title: Integrated measurement: the ordered setup command, end to end, for the six criteria that span it
summary: TSK-0060, INTEGRATED. The ordered setup command, measured end to end through `main()` against real projects, for the six criteria that span the whole command. The implementation is everything from e808b96 to 9510d6e; the sha256 of each file is in the facts. ACC-0085, THE PATHS BEFORE THE FIRST LASTING WRITE. A project-local run prints the canonical tool root, project root, content root, settings path and runtime state path in its first five lines, and the install seam captures the project tree at the moment the bootstrap ran: byte-identical to its pre-run state. An EXTERNAL run is the harder case, because a per-user root is keyed by the project's committed id — so the id is derived in memory, the exact path is printed, and the identity phase is handed THAT id to commit. Measured in a child with every filesystem call recorded from before the command starts: the line naming the external path is printed after ZERO writes to the project, and the id in it is the id the run then committed. A `--project-root` that disagrees with the resolved content owner refuses with both printed, having written nothing. ACC-0106, NO SECRET AND NO ABSOLUTE PATH IN WHAT IS COMMITTED. A complete run against an environment-authenticated provider — asserted from the preflight's own line, since a stored credential would be a different arrangement — with research enabled and its connection checked. The file set is what THIS RUN added or changed: git's own answer before and after, NUL-delimited so a newline in a path cannot read as two entries, with the rename form handled — rather than a list written in the test that would pass forever while the command grew a file nobody added to it. A file the operator writes before the run, carrying a key and a path of its own, is not in that set, which is how the boundary is observable rather than merely intended. Each file is read and asserted to carry no credential, nothing derived from one (sha256 in hex and base64, base64 of the key, a prefix of it), no authorisation header, no path belonging to this machine, and not even the NAMES of the credential variables. `.pi/settings.json` and `.pi/kiln.json` are asserted by name to be in that set; the ignored consent and compatibility records are asserted not to be. EVERY entry in that set is read: there is no exemption list, and an entry that is not a regular file fails, because passing over what a scan cannot read is how a scan stops being one. The fixture's `.planning` link is not in the set at all — it is in the before and the after alike. Absolute paths are checked by shape as well as by value, which is what catches the likeliest real leak: a generator interpolating the checkout it was run from. ONE THING THE SCAN CANNOT PROVE BY DELETION. Removing the leak scan's assertions fails nothing, because nothing currently leaks — a scan bites when there is something to find. What proves it works is injecting leaks: a credential variable's name in settings, an absolute path in a generated document, and the research key in the project record are each caught. ACC-0107, ONE IDENTITY AND THE STATE LIBRARY'S OWN CHOICES. The id is minted once and reused, with the journal gone when the run completes. A project with no coverage is shown exactly the three choices the state library returns, with the ignore block's own bytes; answering nothing, `stop`, `user-state` or anything unrecognised stops with nothing written; and a non-interactive run refuses on the same object with no `.pi`, no content root and no ignore file. External state is offered, which AST-0047 (on EVD-0081) permits: pi 0.84.4 relocates session transcripts through `--session-dir` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, so the per-user root is reachable without committing an absolute path — and a run in that mode commits no `sessionDir` at all. ACC-0043, BYTE-IDENTICAL ON A RERUN. A second run naming nothing reads back the committed selection and this host's approval of it, asks no question, and leaves every file byte-identical — the whole tree by digest, not a reported status — including the settings file, the ignore block, the identity file and the generated content. A third run leaves `.pi/kiln.json`'s mtime untouched, so nothing is rewritten with identical bytes. The compatibility record is byte-identical too, and the check is not run again. ACC-0045, BOTH INTERRUPTION WINDOWS, BY KILLING A RUN. Inside the bootstrap, which runs before any journal exists: a real child is killed mid-install, the project is byte-identical afterwards, no `.pi` survives, and an ordinary rerun — no `--resume`, because there is nothing to resume — completes. After the journal opens: a real child is killed during the trust phase, and what it left records the phase IN FLIGHT as running, which is only true because that status is written before the work; the journal carries an exact resume command naming this project, and the arguments are PARSED OUT OF THAT COMMAND rather than typed beside it — so a command naming another project, omitting `--resume`, or absent altogether each fail the control — and running them completes the remaining phases and leaves no journal. A failure in an agent phase leaves the scaffold: a declined inspection, an unconfirmed model, a denied or failed live check each report partial setup with the project valid. THAT MEASUREMENT FOUND A DEFECT, IN BOTH WINDOWS. A killed run leaves its lockfile, and the stale window that protects waiters from a slow holder is two minutes — so every rerun after a kill refused for two minutes on a lock held by a process that no longer exists. Setup now clears such a lock before any run waits on it, and the safety is in what it still refuses: another machine's lock, an unreadable one, and one whose pid is alive are each left where they are, so two live setups exclude each other exactly as before. REVIEW OF THIS RECORD FOUND A SECOND DEFECT IN THAT FIX, AND THE CONTROL WRITTEN FOR THE SECOND FOUND A THIRD. Clearing a dead owner's lock by reading it and then unlinking it is two writers: two recoveries starting together both read the dead owner, the first unlinks and acquires, and the second unlinks THAT lock — the live one — and acquires it as well. Every rerun takes this path, so it was not a contrived case. The first answer was to claim the file by rename, which cannot be shared, and to judge it again after claiming. FOUR RACING RECOVERIES, ADDED TO CONTROL THAT, FAILED IN CI ON THE FIRST RUN: a recovery that glimpsed the dead owner, and only then renamed, moved a lock somebody had legitimately acquired in between — and although the re-judge put it back, a waiter created its own lock over the free name while it was gone. Two holders again, from the fix's own window. Removing somebody else's lock is now serialised: a breaker takes a gate beside the lock, and the judgement that acts is made inside it, where a lockfile cannot turn from a dead owner's into a live one's — creating one requires it to be absent, making it absent requires removing it, and the only removers are its own holder, dead by assumption, and a breaker, which is here. Both break paths take it, the recovery's and the waiter's stale break, because either one alone leaves the same window. A gate whose holder died inside it is reclaimed by age and death together, and by rename, so one killed recovery cannot block every later one, while a gate somebody took a moment ago — including one they have not finished writing — is left alone. The four racers run again, a second recovery and a waiter each refuse to clear a lock somebody else is clearing, and four mutations — removing either gate, never reclaiming an abandoned one, reclaiming without regard to age — are each caught. ACC-0108, TRUST OBTAINED AND NEVER ASSUMED. An interactive run prints the canonical project directory the decision applies to and asks; `--trust approve` records an approval with no prompt and answers over a recorded decision; a run with nobody to ask refuses WITHOUT REACHING THE QUESTION, measured as zero questions asked. Only an explicit yes approves and only an explicit no denies — a closed input, an empty line and an unreadable answer each leave the store with no decision. A denial is reported as not ready, the agent is never described as usable, nothing is registered, the journal is removed, the scaffold that survives is put through Kiln's own plan linter rather than declared valid because its files exist, AND THE BROWSER-ONLY ROUTE IS SERVED: the application is started against that denied project and asked for a page, which returns a rendered document. Content that validates does not establish that a server can read it. An unapproved project loads none of the package's tools, which is the same fact from Pi's side. WHAT THE WHOLE COMMAND DOES, IN ONE SENTENCE PER PHASE, IS IN THE SLICE RECORDS: EVD-0133 (the order, the built-ins-only graph, the locked install), EVD-0134 (the pinned runtime, trust, registration), EVD-0135 (consent before any read, discovery, selection, the credential contract, research), EVD-0136 (the zero-cost preflight, the separately approved live check, the read-back) and EVD-0137 (the selected content root, the per-user root, the declared custom provider, the exit codes). LIMITS. Nothing billable is contacted anywhere: the one real canary in the suite answers to a loopback server the test runs, every other case injects its runner, the research probe answers through an injected adapter, and npm is a seam in every case — what the bootstrap does is asserted by its arguments, its confinement and the lockfile digest either side. `ACC-0108`'s browser-only route is served for real, but only as this application serving a page: `npm start`'s production path, which installs and builds first, is not exercised. The canary's real request against a real provider, and a real `npm ci` against a registry, remain outside this suite by design.

facts.implementation: the whole of TSK-0060, e808b96 through 9510d6e
facts.tests: test/setup-command.test.mjs: 48 tests against real projects, two of which kill a real child, one of which races four recoveries for one lock, one of which runs the real canary against a loopback server, one of which serves the browser-only route, and one of which runs the command through PowerShell
facts.acc-0085: the five paths in the first five lines with the project tree unchanged at the install; the external path printed after zero writes, naming the id the run then committed; a project-root disagreement refused with both printed
facts.acc-0106: the set is what the run added or changed, from NUL-delimited git status before and after, every entry read with no exemption list; no credential, derived value, authorisation header, absolute path by value or by shape, or credential-variable name in any of it; .pi/settings.json and .pi/kiln.json in the set by name; consent and compatibility records not in it; a file the operator wrote first not in it either
facts.acc-0107: the id minted once and reused, the journal gone on completion, the state library's three choices with the block's bytes, a non-interactive refusal before any runtime file, and external state offered on AST-0047's relocation support
facts.acc-0043: a rerun asks nothing and leaves the whole tree byte-identical, including the compatibility record; a third run leaves the identity file's mtime untouched
facts.acc-0045: both windows by killing a real child: byte-identical project and an ordinary rerun after a bootstrap kill; the in-flight phase and an exact resume command after a post-journal kill, with the arguments PARSED OUT OF that command completing the run
facts.acc-0108: the canonical directory shown and asked about; --trust approve without a prompt; a run with nobody to ask refusing with zero questions; only an explicit yes or no recorded; a denial leaving a scaffold that passes Kiln's plan linter, a project Pi loads no tools for, and a browser-only route that serves it a page
facts.defect-found-by-this-measurement: three, all in the lock, each found by the control written for the one before it: a killed run's lockfile made every rerun wait out the two-minute stale window; clearing it by read-then-unlink lets two recoveries both acquire; and claiming it by rename moves a lock that went live in the meantime, leaving the name free for a waiter while it is put back. Breaking is now serialised behind a gate beside the lock, taken by the recovery path and the waiter's stale break alike, with the judgement made inside it and an abandoned gate reclaimed by age and death together.
facts.no-billable-request: the one real canary answers to a loopback server; every other canary is injected; the research probe is an injected adapter; npm is a seam
facts.full-suite-local: npm test on Windows: 1611 tests, 1606 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped
facts.ci-run: GitHub Actions run 35915409467 at 9510d6e, attempt 1, no job re-run, all four cells succeeded, 0 failures in any cell. The run at 00776db, which this record first described, also passed all four cells.
facts.flake-seen-once: test/f119-query-diagnostic.test.mjs asserts that no snapshot carries the digits of a process-table row, and one local run failed it because a millisecond timing happened to contain them. It is unrelated to this task and passed on the next run; recorded here rather than left unsaid.

omissions.reason: No billable request and no registry install: the one real canary answers to a loopback server, other canaries and the research probe are injected, and npm is a seam whose arguments, confinement and lockfile digest are what is asserted.

ACC-0108's route is exercised by serving the application against the denied project and fetching a page. What is not exercised is `npm start`'s production path — `bin/start-shell.mjs`, which installs and builds before serving — because a test may not run an install.
